source.snippet: I have Email-to-Case set up with several routing addresses, each mapped to its own queue/case record type. The problem: if someone sends (or CCs) an email to more than one of these routing addresses at the same time, Salesforce creates a separate case for each matching address — so one email can spawn 2, 3, or more duplicate cases, all referencing the same message. What I'd like is one of the following: Only create a case from the first matching address, or merge all created cases into one, or detect and suppress the duplicate after creation.

problem_statement: Salesforce Email-to-Case creates duplicate cases when a single inbound email is addressed to multiple routing addresses, causing support queue pollution and agent confusion that requires manual deduplication effort.
target_segment: Salesforce admins and support operations managers at B2B companies running Email-to-Case for customer support
notes: Business buyer is clear: Salesforce-using support org spending agent time on duplicate triage. No explicit 'I'd pay' but Salesforce ecosystem has high willingness-to-pay for AppExchange solutions. Single question but precise and technical, suggesting practitioner with real production pain.
